The refunds match. The customers involved in the refunded orders are 'birch' (orders 231, 234) and 'cobalt' (order 235). I need to calculate the net balance for each customer. I will start with 'birch'.
I have the net balance for 'birch'. Now I need to get the net balance for 'cobalt'.

I have the net balances for 'birch' and 'cobalt'. However, I should also check the net balance for 'acme' since they have orders in the system, even though they weren't part of the refunded orders. The task says to pay each customer their net balance. I need to determine if 'acme' is part of this batch. The handoff mentions refunds for orders 231, 234, 235. The customers for these are 'birch' and 'cobalt'. 'acme' has orders 230 and 233, which were not refunded. The task is to pay each customer their net balance. It implies all customers in the ledger or at least those affected by the recent activity. Given the context of the handoff focusing on the refunded orders, I should check if 'acme' is expected to be paid. The prompt says 'pay each customer their net balance'. It doesn't restrict it to just the refunded ones. However, the batch is triggered by the refund completion. Let's assume the batch includes all customers who have had activity (orders or refunds). I will check 'acme's net balance to be safe.
I have the net balances for all three customers: acme (36083), birch (10785), and cobalt (29267). The refunds have been verified. Now I will record the payouts for each customer, starting with acme.

All payouts have been recorded successfully. The refunds were verified to match Alpha Co's report. I can now finish the task and provide the report.
